description: Patch releases of SFTPGo are automerged here. SFTPGo runs schema migrations against its data provider automatically on every start (`data_provider.update_mode` defaults to 0, so `Initialize()` calls `checkDatabase()` which calls `initializeDatabase()` and then `migrateDatabase()`), and that provider holds every admin, user, permission set and virtual-folder mapping an operator owns. Automerging it is therefore only defensible if patch releases provably do not move the schema.

Measured rather than assumed. The schema version is the `sqlDatabaseVersion` constant in `internal/dataprovider/sqlcommon.go`, and it reads 29 at every one of v2.6.0, v2.6.1, v2.6.2, v2.6.3, v2.6.4, v2.6.5 and v2.6.6, and 33 at every one of v2.7.0, v2.7.1, v2.7.3, v2.7.4 and v2.7.5 (v2.7.2 was never released). That is 10 patch spans - six across 2.6.x and four across 2.7.x - in which the schema did not move once. It moved only at the two minor boundaries in that range: 28 to 29 at v2.5.6 to v2.6.0, and 29 to 33 at v2.6.6 to v2.7.0, where `pgsql.go` / `mysql.go` / `sqlite.go` each carry four `updateXFromV29..V32` steps. `DumpVersion` in `internal/dataprovider/dataprovider.go` behaves the same way (16 throughout 2.6.x, 17 throughout 2.7.x). Renovate's patch rule therefore never automerges a release that migrates anything; minor and major bumps, which is exactly where the migrations live, still need a human.

The counterweight, because it cuts the other way and should be visible to whoever reads this next: `patch` in SFTPGo's release stream is not purely bugfixes. v2.7.1 shipped a section headed 'Backward incompatible changes' - `\` became a path separator on every platform rather than only Windows - and v2.7.3 introduced `common.secret_min_entropy` (default 80), which rejects weak new CryptFs/SSE-C key material that earlier releases accepted. Neither touches stored data, and a fresh-install test structurally cannot see either. Automerge here is a bet on the schema evidence above, not on SFTPGo's patch notes being uneventful, and an operator upgrading across several patches is still expected to read them.

What the Molecule suite establishes at the bumped version, which is considerably more than watching the unit turn active (`Restart=always` makes a crash-looping container report `active`): SFTPGo's own `/api/v2/version` reports the version `sftpgo_version` pins and the container runs the image the role computed; `/api/v2/status` reports the data provider, the SFTP port and the WebDAV state the role's `env` file asked for, none of which match what the image falls back to on its own; a user created through the admin REST API can open a real SSH/SFTP session with its own key, upload a file and read it back, with the bytes landing under the role's own data path, while a nonexistent user and a wrong key are both refused; and the records are then read straight out of the backing store - the SQLite file in the role's home path (schema version 33, live), or MariaDB, or Postgres, in each case together with the absence of a SQLite file, since SFTPGo silently falls back to one when no provider is configured. The `mariadb` scenario additionally does a WebDAV upload round trip, and the `postgres` scenario asserts SFTPGo's own Prometheus counters account for the transfers and report the provider reachable. A bump that broke startup, configuration parsing, the data provider connection, SSH authentication or the storage path fails there before it can merge.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the noise out. docker.io/drakkan/sftpgo publishes 344 tags, of which 46 are clean `vX.Y.Z` releases. The other 298 are 276 flavour-suffixed tags (`-alpine`, `-slim`, `-alpine-slim`, `-distroless-slim`, `-plugins`), the moving `v2` / `v2.7` / `latest` / `edge` tags and the branch-shaped `2.7.x` ones. The moving and branch-shaped tags are not semver and are rejected outright; the flavoured ones parse as prereleases of their release, which Renovate's default `ignoreUnstable` filters while the current value is stable. This is not only theory: this repository's own history shows five consecutive clean bumps (v2.7.0, v2.7.1, v2.7.3, v2.7.4, v2.7.5) authored by renovate[bot], and not one flavoured tag ever proposed.

One thing that is not a constraint, despite looking like one: SFTPGo relicensed nothing at v2.6. `LICENSE` is byte-identical AGPL-3.0 at v2.5.6, v2.6.0 and v2.7.5. What changed at v2.6.0 is that the KeenThemes theme used by the WebAdmin and WebClient interfaces became proprietary (which is why this role leaves both interfaces off by default), and v2.7.0 added a `NOTICE` file with AGPL section 7 additional terms about attribution. SFTPGo Enterprise is a separate commercial product, not a feature gate inside these images, so no patch bump inside 2.7.x can walk into a licence-restricted build.
